problem: Given that $a=⟨1,-3,2⟩,$ $b=⟨2,-1,-1⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,-3,0⟩,$ find $a\cdot (b\times c)$ using the definition of the scalar triple product.

feedback.worked_solution:
Substituting given vectors into the formula for the scalar triple product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨-\sqrt{3},0,-2⟩\cdot ⟨-\sqrt{3},10,-10⟩ \\  & =(-\sqrt{3})\cdot (-\sqrt{3})+0\cdot 10+(-2)\cdot (-10) \\  & =3+0+20 \\  & =23.\end{aligned}
$$
